t: Here, on Leadenhall Street in the City, stood East India House, the London headquarters of the East India Company. Much of British India was governed from this building until the Crown took over the company's possessions in 1858. The Company first occupied an Elizabethan mansion on the site in 1648. It was rebuilt in 1726 to 1729, then remodelled and extended between 1796 and 1800 by Henry Holland and Richard Jupp, who was surveyor to the Company. The building was demolished in 1861, and Lloyd's of London's headquarters now stands on the site.
